column4: Visit note | 2026-03-03 03:30 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Bithi Bhattacharya, 42, female. Mrs. Bhattacharya reports she has itchy eyes and a runny nose, with a constantly blocked nose and snoring with little sneezing. Her symptoms flare each spring in Old Dhaka. She works as a homemaker and lives with her family. She has no known comorbidities and denies fever or facial pain. On examination: about 14 sneezing fits a day, BP 130/85 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, weight 65 kg. The nasal mucosa appears pale and boggy. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. She was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2026-03-10 04:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Fariha Bhuiyan, 61, female. Mrs. Bhuiyan presents complaining of a tingling sensation like pins and needles, burning in both feet, and numbness in the toes. She mentions it has been worse since walking barefoot at home in Rampura. She is an NGO field officer and spends long hours standing. She has no chronic comorbidities. On examination: reduced sensation at 5 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 127/82 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 91 kg. Ankle jerks are sluggish bilaterally. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. She was advised to check her feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep her blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2026-03-15 04:30 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Mitu Munshi, 64, female. On examination: reduced sensation at 5 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 124/73 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 71 kg. Cranial nerves are intact. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. She was advised to check her feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep her blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2026-03-15 04:30 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Faruk Kabir, 69, male. Mr. Kabir attends for review concerning his sleep, stating he wakes up tired and experiences persistent worry about sleep. He mentions his sleep trouble began after a newborn arrived in the family in Khilgaon. He works as a shopkeeper. He has a known comorbidity of Bronchial asthma. He reports no daytime hallucinations or focal weakness. On examination: Insomnia Severity Index score 15, BP 126/85 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 93 kg. Chest examination reveals clear air entry with no wheeze today. Assessment: Chronic insomnia. Plan: chronic follow-up; continue current medicines, no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. He was advised to keep fixed sleep and wake times, avoid screens for an hour before bed, and avoid tea after 4 PM. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a sleep diary.

Visit note | 2026-03-22 03:30 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Tamanna Sheikh, 29, female. Miss Sheikh complains of painful cramps in the first days of each period and nausea with the pain, noting that pain spreads to the lower back and thighs with vomiting. She states the discomfort has been worse since a stressful family move to Shyamoli. She works as a delivery rider. She has a comorbidity of Hypothyroidism. She denies abnormal intermenstrual bleeding. On examination: pain score 7/10, BP 127/73 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 72 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild suprapubic tenderness. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: a pelvic ultrasound if the pain worsens; no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. She was advised to use a hot water bottle, do light exercise, and keep a period diary. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2026-03-23 10:30 AM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Habiba Dewan, 20, female. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. She was advised to use a hot water bottle, do light exercise, and keep a period diary. Follow-up in 3 months with the period diary.

Visit note | 2026-03-28 12:30 PM | Dr. Shamima Nasrin, Ophthalmology | Patient: Laila Islam, 75, female. Mrs. Islam describes her symptoms as worse in air conditioning, accompanied by long hours of screen time, and gritty burning eyes. She notes her trouble began after long gaming sessions at home in Uttara. She is a homemaker. She has a comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies sudden visual loss or severe eye pain. On examination: tear break-up time 4 seconds, BP 128/74 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 73 kg. Corneas are clear bilaterally with mild conjunctival injection. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: referral to Neurology in this clinic for further assessment; no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. She was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up after the Neurology review.

Visit note | 2026-03-28 03:30 PM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Sajjad Ahmed, 21, male. Mr. Ahmed reports experiencing a sour taste in his mouth and a burning sensation behind his breastbone after meals. He states it has been worse after weeks of fried snacks at tea stalls in Dhanmondi. He is a homemaker. He has no reported comorbidities. On examination: BMI 31.7, BP 132/86 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 68 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild epigastric tenderness. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests unless symptoms persist; no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. He was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2026-03-31 11:30 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Hossain Haque, 61, male. Mr. Haque complains of band-like pressure around the head, neck tightness, and stress. He mentions his discomfort began after a stressful house move to Rajshahi. He works as a fisherman. He has no chronic comorbidities. On examination: pain score 4/10, BP 121/78 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 49 kg. Neurological examination shows no focal deficits or cranial nerve abnormalities. Assessment: Tension-type headache. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests; no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. He was advised to take screen breaks every hour, do neck stretches, and sleep seven hours. Follow-up after the test results are ready.
